claim: Video shows “thousands of Christians in France gathered to pray after Olympics opening mocked Jesus Christ.”
explanation: "Breaking: Thousands of Christians in France gathered to pray after Olympics opening mocked Jesus Christ," read text across a video shared in a July 29 Instagram post. Some X users shared a different video and claimed it, too, showed people gathered in Paris for a "worship service" in response to the Olympics opening ceremony. Nevertheless, some social media users shared a video that they claimed showed thousands gathering in France to pray in response.

claim: Sean “Diddy” Combs wrote the book “The Adrenochrome Witch.”
explanation: We found no book listing by Combs or about an adrenochrome witch when searching Barnes & Noble’s website, but doing a Google search for the title led us to a sample page on Barnes & Noble’s "Nook for Web" site, which allows users to read e-books and e-book samples on a computer. "This is not an authentic book and we do not have it listed on our website," Barnes & Noble said in a statement to PolitiFact. The sample page used the same image of Combs and said "The Adrenochrome Witch by Diddy."

claim: "ABC elimina a los moderadores del debate David Muir y Linsey Davis".
explanation: Una búsqueda en Google y en la base de datos Nexis no mostró noticias sobre el supuesto despido de Muir y Davis por parte de ABC News. Captura de pantalla de la publicación en Facebook. El artículo también dice que Elon Musk, propietario de X y director general de Tesla, y Megyn Kelly, presentadora de un programa de entrevistas conservador, comentaron en internet sobre el despido.

claim: Says Wisconsin GOP U.S. Senate candidate Eric Hovde "brags about being in the 1%."
explanation: The Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee claimed Hovde "brags about being in the 1%" in an ad based on a quote from 12 years ago. The committee put out an attack ad against Wisconsin Republican senatorial candidate Eric Hovde that says Hovde "brags about being in the 1%." Did Hovde brag about being part of the 1%?

claim: JD Vance “literally wrote the foreword for the architect of the Project 2025 agenda."
explanation: Walz said Vance "literally wrote the foreword for the architect of the Project 2025 agenda." Vance wrote the forward for a book authored by Roberts, the Heritage Foundation’s president and a Project 2025 leader. Vance literally, literally wrote the foreword for the architect of the Project 2025 agenda," Walz said Aug. 6 in Philadelphia, as Vice President Kamala Harris stood behind him.

claim: A plane crashed into the Milad Tower, July 31, 2024.
explanation: A Facebook post shows a video of a plane seemingly crashing into a tower and exploding. PolitiFact found no credible media reports of a plane crashing into Milad Tower in 2024. On his Instagram and TikTok accounts we found the same video of the plane crashing into a tower, posted July 13.

claim: Former President Donald Trump could have destroyed the Affordable Care Act, but “he chose to build upon (it)."
explanation: Vance’s assertion that Trump as president took steps to build upon the Affordable Care Act and protect the health coverage of 20 million Americans is simply not supported by the record. Trump said of the Affordable Care Act, "I saved it." Meanwhile, the Trump administration expanded access to some kinds of less expensive  health coverage that isn’t compliant with Affordable Care Act rules, including short-term plans that generally have more restrictions on care and can leave consumers with surprise medical bills.

claim: Ryan Routh's Instagram bio says he is a "proud LGBTQ+ member"
explanation: Although much news coverage of Routh included coverage of his posts on X, detailed news reports from several major news outlets do not mention an Instagram account or any connection to the LGBTQ+ community. Routh’s social media accounts on Facebook and X  nor his self-published book mentioned LGBTQ+ identity. Immediately after reports surfaced Routh as the possible suspect, PolitiFact reporters searched for social media accounts under his name and found only a Facebook and X account.

claim: Taylor Swift “lost 17 million followers by endorsing Kamala.”
explanation: "Taylor Swift loses more than 100 million followers on Instagram after Harris endorsement," a Sept. 11 post said. "Taylor Swift loses 50 million Instagram followers," a Sept. 17 Facebook post said. "Taylor Swift had 301 million Instagram followers last week, a Sept. 16 Instagram post said.

claim: “Kamala Harris has promised amnesty for the 10 million illegals she allowed in as border czar, making them eligible for Social Security. Studies warn this will lead to cuts in your Social Security benefits."
explanation: The Center for Immigration Studies argued that providing a pathway to citizenship for the millions of immigrants who are in the U.S. illegally would harm Social Security partly because it would reverse the trend of having more beneficiaries than workers paying into the program. However, it published a 2021 report that said that providing a pathway to citizenship for the millions of immigrants who are living in the U.S. illegally would weaken Social Security’s solvency. And Harris has not announced a plan that would provide immigrants who entered the U.S. illegally under Biden a pathway to citizenship.

claim: Kamala Harris was “Indian all the way, and then all of a sudden, she made a turn and she went, she became a Black person.”
explanation: Trump said Harris was Indian and then "made a turn" and "became a Black person." Harris said she grew up embracing her Indian culture while proudly living as a Black girl. Harris has embraced her Black identity and multicultural background in several ways.

claim: Says Elon Musk said on X, “Go to my crypto project.”
explanation: Searching more broadly online for evidence that Musk said this, we found only social media posts such as this Threads post and a YouTube video titled, "Free bitcoin promo code scam explained." We rate claims Musk posted this cryptocurrency message on X False. A recent Threads post purports to show a billboard in New York’s Times Square with a message from X owner Elon Musk: "Go to my crypto project BEDXERS.COM Enter my promo code 31muskxx Take 0.31 BTC."

claim: Photos that show lists of school names are “school shooting lists.”
explanation: The list in the Facebook post featuring the Georgia schools even has a title that says "2024 Title I Schools Schoolwide (SWP) and Targeted Assisted (TA)," and the list by that name can be found on the Georgia Department of Education website. Spokespeople for the Georgia Department of Education and New Mexico Public Education Department declined to comment on the lists in the social media posts. Meghan Frick with the Georgia Department of Education referred us to law enforcement agencies including the Georgia Bureau of Investigations "given the sensitivity of the situation."

claim: A video shows “triggered Kamala Harris walks out on Charlamagne Tha God after he exposed Joe Biden’s dementia.”
explanation: The video showed McKelvey asking Harris, "Is it Joe Manchin or Joe Biden, Madam Vice President?" Is it Joe Manchin or Joe Biden?" It is Joe Biden."

claim: Video shows “geoengineering happening” as Hurricane Milton approaches Florida.
explanation: But the video does not show pre-Hurricane Milton clouds over Florida. This video doesn’t show geoengineering occurring as Hurricane Milton approaches Florida. The clouds in the video don’t show a hurricane.

claim: In Springfield, Ohio, “murders are up by 81%.”
explanation: Longer-term data, from 2013 to 2022, reported by the Springfield police to the FBI, shows that the number of homicides has fluctuated in Springfield without a clear trend. For example, the Springfield News-Sun reported that there were nine homicides in 2021; WHIO-TV said there were 12 homicides in 2021. Data reported to the Ohio Incident Based Reporting System showed that from 2021 to 2023, murders in Springfield rose from five to nine — an 80% increase.

claim: “Kurt Russell forms a new non-woke actors alliance with Roseanne Barr and Tim Allen.”
explanation: "Kurt Russell forms a new non-woke actors alliance with Roseanne Barr and Tim Allen," an Aug. 27 Facebook post said. But these actors didn’t form a "non-woke actors alliance," as a recent Facebook post claims. This post was flagged as part of Meta’s efforts to combat false news and misinformation on its News Feed.

claim: Says immigrants with temporary protections in Springfield, Ohio, are “illegal immigrants.”
explanation: But immigration law experts said that, once immigrants have Temporary Protected Status protections, they are in the U.S. legally — regardless of how they entered the U.S. before receiving it. People can apply for Temporary Protected Status whether they entered the U.S. legally or illegally. Citizenship and Immigration Services, an agency within the department, about the immigration status of people with Temporary Protected Status and humanitarian parole.

claim: U.S. Sen. Sherrod Brown “supported allowing puberty blockers and sex-change surgeries for minor children.”
explanation: Gender-affirming care is an individualized health care model that prioritizes encouraging and supporting a person’s gender identity — it  is more than puberty blockers and surgery. The Senate Leadership Fund said in an ad that Brown "supported allowing puberty blockers and sex-change surgeries for minor children." The Senate Leadership Fund supplied a closed-caption transcript of the news segment, in which a reporter asked Brown about legislation from Sen. JD Vance, R-Ohio, that aimed to ban gender-affirming care for minors.

claim: The proposal to put golf courses, hotels in Florida state parks “was something that was leaked. … a lot of that stuff was half-baked and was not ready for prime time.”
explanation: The Florida Department of State sent a notification Aug. 20 announcing plans to hold Aug. 27 public meetings about the proposed plans across the state. The department canceled the public meetings and withdrew the plans for golf courses at Jonathan Dickinson State Park. DeSantis said the environmental protection agency’s proposal to put golf courses, hotels in Florida state parks "was something that was leaked.

claim: Video shows Jordan Peterson making disparaging remarks about Chinese food
explanation: We rate the claim that this video shows Peterson making disparaging remarks about Chinese food  Pants on Fire! A video of Canadian celebrity psychologist Jordan Peterson appears to show him making disparaging remarks about Chinese cuisine. The Facebook video directed viewers to purchase a book promoting herbal tablets.

claim: Sen. Bob Casey “voted to sell American oil to China.”
explanation: Casey voted against a procedural measure that would have allowed consideration of an amendment to ban exports of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to China. Casey voted no on a procedural vote about whether to consider an amendment that would have limited foreign exports of oil from the reserve. Casey never participated in a Senate vote that led to the sale of American oil to China.

claim: “Scientists at Exeter University have reconstructed this 3D model of how Moses might have looked.”
explanation: In 2022, PolitIFact fact-checked a claim that Stanford University scientists published a 3D image of what Joseph of Nazareth might have looked like: a rendering of André René Roussimof, a French former professional wrestler and actor known as Andre the Giant. "Scientists at Exeter University have reconstructed this 3D model of how Moses might have looked," the July 31 post said. We found nothing on the website of the University of Exeter, in the United Kingdom, to support the claim that scientists there rendered a 3D model of Moses.

claim: In Manchester, N.H., gubernatorial candidate Joyce Craig “pushed for a city sales tax. Then, Joyce Craig overrode the tax cap and tried to raise taxes six times.”
explanation: In 2019, the year the ad says Craig "overrode the tax cap," aldermen had a veto-proof supermajority, meaning Craig could not have overridden their vote to exceed the tax cap. Craig introduced the city sales tax idea a decade before her mayorship, when she was on the school board. The Craig campaign disputed the tax attacks.

claim: When Haitians go to school in Springfield, Ohio, they “take the place of our children in school” and “each one will have a private interpreter."
explanation: Springfield schools have hired staff to teach Haitian students and other English language learners, but we found no evidence that each student "will have a private interpreter." Trump said when Haitians go to school in Springfield they "take the place of our children in school" and "each one will have a private interpreter." A school official told the Springfield News-Sun in 2023 that English language learners do not take away from the English language students.

claim: “The most recent State Budget increased funding for the Department of Tourism by 98 percent.”
explanation: Cowles said: "The most recent State Budget increased funding for the Department of Tourism by 98 percent." "The most recent State Budget increased funding for the Department of Tourism by 98 percent," state Sen. One Wisconsin lawmaker says funding for the state’s tourism department is up nearly 100 percent.

claim: First lady Jill Biden led a Cabinet meeting for President Joe Biden and her signature appears on presidential stationery.
explanation: In an email announcing her Sept. 20 schedule, the White House said, "At 11:30 AM, First Lady Jill Biden will join at the top of President Biden’s Cabinet meeting to provide an update on the progress of the White House Initiative on Women’s Health Research." The White House said first lady Jill Biden and the White House Gender Policy Council would lead its Initiative on Women’s Health Research in November 2023. It was Jill Biden’s first Cabinet appearance since Joe Biden took office.

claim: During the 2020 Minnesota riots after George Floyd’s murder, Gov. Tim Walz didn’t call in the National Guard, “so, I sent in the National Guard to save Minneapolis.”
explanation: Trump said that during the 2020 Minnesota riots, Walz didn’t call in the National Guard. Frey said he called Walz on the evening of May 27, 2020, asking him to send in the National Guard and Walz said he would consider it. However, Walz spokesperson Teddy Tschann wrote in a statement to CNN in 2020 that Walz "activated the Minnesota National Guard at the request of the Mayors of Minneapolis and St. Paul, before he talked to the White House."

claim: “Kamala Harris said she will shut down X if elected.”
explanation: The same rule has to apply, which is that there has to be a responsibility that is placed on these social media sites to understand their power. The same rule has to apply, which is that there has to be a responsibility that is placed on these social media sites to understand their power. An Instagram user shared a video Sept. 3 of Harris speaking with the caption, "Kamala Harris says she will shut down X if elected."

claim: President Joe Biden “did a campaign ad at the graves in Arlington in 2020.”
explanation: An X post said that Biden "did a campaign ad at the graves in Arlington in 2020." Biden shared a 2020 campaign ad that included a photo taken at Arlington National Cemetery, but it was taken in 2010 as part of his vice presidential duties, not as part of a campaign activity. "Joe Biden literally did a campaign ad at the graves in Arlington in 2020."

claim: Jon Tester “supported slashing Social Security benefits”
explanation: Meanwhile, several groups that advocate for Social Security and its beneficiaries have endorsed Tester: the National Committee to Preserve Social Security and Medicare, the Montana Alliance for Retired Americans and Social Security Works. Sheehy’s statement also ignores Tester’s stated position of supporting Social Security as is, and his endorsement by several Social Security advocacy groups. Sheehy said Tester "supported slashing Social Security benefits."

claim: NFL’s Philadelphia Eagles endorsed Kamala Harris for president.
explanation: Have the NFL’s Philadelphia Eagles endorsed Vice President Kamala Harris as president? Eagles spokesperson Bob Lange told PolitiFact the team’s statement referred to the Harris bus stop ads. We rate the claim that the Eagles endorsed Kamala Harris for president False.

claim: Food and Drug Administration approval for updated COVID-19 vaccines requires a public health emergency declaration.
explanation: That’s because the COVID-19 public health emergency and the COVID-19 emergency use authorization were declared by Health and Human Services under two distinct laws. An emergency use declaration doesn’t hinge on a public health emergency declaration and it can stay in effect after a public health emergency ends, the FDA said. The claim that the FDA shouldn’t be able to approve the new COVID-19 vaccines because there is no public health emergency and that other treatments are available is False.

claim: U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers “believes he should make that decision” about whether to end pregnancies.
explanation: Rogers supported strict abortion bans in the past, and said he believed the government had a responsibility to restrict abortion access. Slotkin campaign spokesperson Antoine Givens said Rogers supported abortion restrictions at every point in his congressional career, and his voting record shows he believes the government should restrict abortion rights. More recently, though, Rogers has said that he respects the constitutional protections for abortion access that Michigan voters approved in a 2022 referendum, and he said he would not vote to change those protections if elected to the U.S. Senate.

claim: Vice President Kamala Harris is “calling for an end to the child tax credit.”
explanation: In January, Harris lauded the House for passing a bipartisan tax package that includes the child tax credit expansion. Vance said Harris is "calling on ending the child tax credit." Harris called the increased child tax credit "one of the most important, one of the most impactful parts of the American Rescue Plan."

claim: Video shows “FBI finds human remains at a McDonald’s meat supplier.”
explanation: "FBI finds human remains at a McDonald’s meat supplier," read text over several Instagram videos shared Sept. 27 and Sept. 29 that show a television news reporter appearing to break news about the FBI recovering evidence of human remains from a Detroit business. The claim that this video shows the "FBI finds human remains at a McDonald’s meat supplier" is Pants on Fire! The video clip is real, but it does not show a reporter at a McDonald’s meat supplier.

claim: Tim Sheehy “would let politicians like him ban abortion, with no exceptions for rape or to save a woman’s life, and criminalize women.”
explanation: Sheehy has said he supports abortion ban exceptions for rape or to save a pregnant woman’s life. The Tester campaign’s ad says Sheehy "would let politicians like him ban abortion, with no exceptions for rape or to save a woman’s life, and criminalize women." Sheehy would let politicians like him ban abortion, with no exceptions for rape or to save a woman’s life, and criminalize women.

claim: “Vice President, Kamala Harris cast the tie-breaking vote to cut, as you know, Medicare by $273 billion. She cast a vote to cut Medicare.”
explanation: But the government’s spending less on Medicare programs would not amount to the kind of "cut" to Medicare benefits Trump implied, experts told KFF Health News. The analysis Trump cited, per his campaign, said the Inflation Reduction Act’s health care provisions would lower the deficit by $237 billion — not $273 billion, as the former president claimed. "The idea behind drug price negotiation is that Medicare can use its buying power to get a better price than what is currently being negotiated for these drugs," said Juliette Cubanski, deputy director of the program on Medicare policy at KFF, a health information nonprofit that includes KFF Health News.

claim: The Democratic National Convention was “nearly empty” during its first day.
explanation: "The DNC is nearly empty," one person wrote Aug. 19 on Instagram Threads. "The difference between the RNC and DNC is apparent. The post was accompanied with a video of Minyon Moore, the DNC convention committee chair, and Jaime Harrison, the Democratic National Committee chair, speaking to a sparsely populated venue on the convention’s first day.

claim: Video shows “several masked men stormed a local voting station and stole the ballot boxes” in Venezuela’s 2024 election.
explanation: Social media posts claim that a video shows "several masked men stormed a local voting station and stole the ballot boxes" during Venezuela’s 2024 election. Social media posts claim that a video shows people stealing ballot boxes from local election sites. "UNDEMOCRATIC: In Punta Cardón, Falcón State, Venezuela, it is reported that several masked men stormed a local voting station and stole the ballot boxes transporting then to an undisclosed location afterwards," a July 28 X post says, using "then" when it probably meant "them."

claim: “Elon Musk to fund new anti-woke show featuring Tucker Carlson.”
explanation: The SpaceX Fanclub post included in the comments a link to a blog post claiming the new show will be called "Truth Unleashed." "Elon Musk to fund new anti-woke show featuring Tucker Carlson: ‘We need more journalists like Tucker Carlson and less like Rachel Maddow,’" the Sept. 6 post said. The Facebook post sharing the Carlson claim does not say that it’s satire.

claim: “Attorney General Merrick Garland just vetoed charging Ryan Routh with attempted assassination” of Donald Trump.
explanation: The TikTok video’s claim that Garland vetoed an attempted assassination charge against Routh ignores that Garland said the federal investigation of the incident continues. "So, Attorney General Merrick Garland just vetoed charging Ryan Routh with attempted assassination," a man said in a Sept. 18 TikTok video that had nearly 200,000 likes by Sept. 20. But the TikTok videos ignore that the Justice Department said its federal investigation continues, and that more serious charges may come.

claim: Video shows Sean “Diddy” Combs speaking “from prison.”
explanation: "Diddy Combs speaks from prison," a Sept. 26 Instagram post sharing the video said. Combs pleaded not guilty, but a video that purportedly shows him speaking from prison is being mischaracterized on social media. Combs captioned the video, "Diddy Blog #1001 ….

claim: Video shows an Iranian missile attack.
explanation: Other users shared the video on X, also claiming it shows an Iranian missile attack. On one X post, a community note says the footage is from the video game "Wargame: Red Dragon." Screenshot from X But the video predates Iran’s Oct. 1 missile attack.

claim: Hurricane Milton is part of Tampa’s plan to become a “15-minute city.”
explanation: There is no evidence that Hurricane Milton is part of Tampa’s plan to become a "15-minute city." An Oct. 7 Instagram video showed Google search results about Tampa becoming a 15-minute city. As Hurricane Milton moved toward Florida’s west coast, some social media users claimed the hurricane is part of a conspiracy to turn Tampa, Florida, into a "15-minute city."

claim: The Inflation Reduction Act, which Rep. Elissa Slotkin supported, “drove inflation higher.”
explanation: Americans for Prosperity Action said the Slotkin-supported Inflation Reduction Act "drove inflation higher." "Slotkin voted for the $1.2 trillion Inflation Reduction Act that drove inflation higher," the group said in an ad. Despite what the ad claims, though, year-over-year inflation has gone down, not up, since President Joe Biden signed the Inflation Reduction Act into law in August 2022.

claim: Gov. Tim Walz insulted Ann Coulter’s romantic history after she called his son “weird.”
explanation: Walz did not respond to her X post. A Walz spokesperson did not immediately respond when asked whether the post was authentic. Walz has not deleted any posts since Aug. 22, according to Social Blade, a social media analytics website.

claim: Says opponent Sen. Tammy Baldwin “gave our taxpayer money to a transgender-affirming clinic … that does it without even telling parents."
explanation: When asked for the evidence behind the claim, a Hovde spokesperson pointed to the $400,000 in federal money that Baldwin requested from a $1.2 trillion government spending package passed in March for Fitchburg-based Briarpatch Youth Services, which serves runaway and homeless youth in Dane County. Baldwin did secure funds for Briarpatch Youth Services, which has a program for LGBTQ+ youth that doesn’t require parental permission to join. Hovde claimed that Baldwin gave taxpayer money to a transgender-affirming clinic that "does it without even telling parents."

claim: "Tim Walz signed into law driver's licenses for illegal immigrants in Minnesota."
explanation: On March 7, 2023, as Minnesota governor, Walz signed H.F. 4, a bill that expanded access to driver’s licenses to people in the state, regardless of their immigration status. Walz signed a bill in 2023 expanding access to driver’s licenses regardless of immigration status in Minnesota. Tim Walz signed law giving some Minnesota students, including migrants, free in-state tuition

claim: Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz signed “legislation giving free college … to illegal immigrants.”
explanation: Students who are illegally in the U.S. can apply for this tuition aid if they have attended a Minnesota school for at least three years, graduated or received a GED certificate in Minnesota and satisfied other requirements for income and maintaining their school’s GPA standards. The short story: Walz signed a scholarship program into law that covers tuition at Minnesota public colleges and universities for students who meet family income restrictions. In the 2021-22 school year, 314 Minnesotan students received financial aid through the Minnesota Dream Act.

claim: “We have cut the flow of fentanyl by half.”
explanation: Fentanyl seizure data tells us only how much fentanyl was stopped from entering the U.S. Data on fentanyl seizures inside the U.S. is incomplete, Luckey said. But neither data point proves with certainty that the rise in seizures is evidence that fentanyl in the U.S. has been cut in half.

claim: “Estados Unidos decide INVADIR VENEZUELA”.
explanation: Después de la elección presidencial del 28 de julio, el Secretario de Estado de Estados Unidos, Anthony Blinken, expresó preocupación sobre los resultados y pidió la publicación de la tabulación detallada de los votos. (Captura de pantalla de publicación en Facebook) El 30 de julio, el Presidente Joe Biden dijo que habló con el presidente de Brasil sobre asuntos bilaterales y regionales, incluyendo la elección en Venezuela. "Estamos de acuerdo en la necesidad de que las autoridades electorales venezolanas publiquen las cifras de votos completas, transparentes y detalladas, a nivel de los centros de votación.

claim: “ESPN has fired Shannon Sharpe.”
explanation: USA Today Sports and other news outlets reported Sept. 12 that ESPN said Sharpe would continue to appear on the network. But ESPN told PolitiFact on Sept. 13 that Sharpe would continue to appear on the network as normally scheduled. He said he had talked to ESPN about the event and would continue to appear on the network.

claim: Video clips show Hurricane Milton hitting Florida “with wind speed 185 mph as Category 5”
explanation: Hurricane Milton left a path of destruction as it made landfall Oct. 9 along Florida’s west coast. Hurricane Milton strengthened to a Category 5 storm when it was still over water, but by the time it hit Florida’s central west coast, it was a Category 3. An Oct. 9 TikTok video, accompanied by text that read, "Hurricane Milton just (made) landfall in Florida with wind speed 185 mph as Category 5," claimed to show the storm's destruction.

claim: Image shows the projected trajectory for a Hurricane Nadine is “the same path as Helene.”
explanation: The projected trajectory looks like the same path as Helene because it is an image of Hurricane Helene’s projected trajectory. We rate claims this image shows the projected trajectory for a hurricane called Nadine False. The post included an image of a "First Alert Weather" map that says "Tropical Tracker" and shows the projected trajectory of a storm with wind gusts of up to 130 miles per hour.

claim: El director general de la Organización Mundial de la Salud "dice que ya no es emergencia sanitaria la viruela del mono" en 2024.
explanation: El director general de la OMS anunció una nueva emergencia de salud pública de importancia internacional en 2024 Un vocero de la OMS le confirmó a PolitiFact que el director general de la OMS declaró el aumento de casos de mpox como una emergencia de salud pública de importancia internacional en agosto de 2024. Tedros declaró la emergencia debido a la rápida propagación de casos de la mpox en el este de la República Democrática del Congo, la detección de la enfermedad en países vecinos, y por la posibilidad de una mayor propagación dentro y fuera de África. El video en Instagram es de mayo de 2023, cuando Tedros anunció el fin de la emergencia de salud pública internacional del mpox declarada en el 2022.

claim: World Economic Forum “document confirms 6 billion humans will die in 2025.”
explanation: We found no reputable news organizations or credible information showing that a World Economic Forum document "confirm(ed) 6 billion humans" — or over 70% of the world’s population — will die in 2025. However, the article does not identify or link to any World Economic Forum document that meets that description. A supposed document from the World Economic Forum.

claim: Video shows a missile strike on Israel.
explanation: We rate the claim that a video shows an Iranian missile strike on Israel False. The lights in the media office’s video resemble those in the Instagram post. We geolocated the video and confirmed it shows Dubai Marina, an area on the Persian Gulf in Dubai, United Arab Emirates.

claim: An image shows Taylor Swift responding to Elon Musk's X post about giving her a child by saying she's happy to take his daughter Vivian and ‘give her all the love and respect she deserves.’
explanation: PolitiFact found no evidence of a response to Musk being shared on any of Swift’s other social media accounts, including Threads, Facebook, Instagram and TikTok. No such post appears on Swift’s X account, with the most recent update, a post she shared June 22, 2024, wishing Prince William a happy birthday. The "Vivian" in the fake Swift post seemingly refers to Vivian Wilson, Musk's transgender daughter, whom the tech CEO said was dead to him after being "killed by the woke mind virus" following her transition.

claim: “Georgia coach Kirby Smart's family ends relationship with Taylor Swift: ‘We do not support her endorsement.’”
explanation: Other social media accounts also shared the claim that the Smart family ended its relationship with Swift, but without a source. Kirby Smart, coach of the University of Georgia’s football team, shared news space with singer-songwriter Taylor Swift in July, when Smart’s wife and children traveled to Amsterdam to see an Eras Tour concert. No credible news outlets have reported on Smart’s family severing ties with Swift, which would be merit coverage considering the attention paid to his family members’ trip to the Netherlands.

claim: Ryan Routh appeared in a Blackrock commercial.
explanation: "The latest Trump would be assassin — Ryan Routh ALSO appeared in a Blackrock Commercial just like Thomas Crooks," a Sept.16 X post reads. After his arrest, social media users shared a video of Routh that they say connects him to BlackRock Inc., a New York-based investment management company. The post is accompanied by a video clip of Routh in the crowd at a rally with an American flag tied around his neck.

claim: “Kamala cast the tiebreaking vote to hire 87,000 new IRS agents to go after your tip income.”
explanation: The claim that the IRS would hire 87,000 IRS agents came from a 2021 Department of Treasury report that said the IRS would use the $80 billion from the Inflation Reduction Act to hire 86,852 full-time employees by 2031. Trump said Harris "cast the tiebreaking vote to hire 87,000 new IRS agents to go after your tip income." In February 2023, the IRS proposed a new tip reporting program that would let service industry employers report tips voluntarily to help with tax compliance.

claim: “Weatherman loses it live on air” during broadcast about Hurricane Helene.
explanation: Hurricane Helene made landfall Sept. 26 in northwestern Florida as a Category 4 storm, but a video that purportedly shows a meteorologist describing Doppler radar imagery as "Satan’s butthole" isn’t an authentic weather broadcast. The person in this video is not meteorologist "Jim Acosted" but comedian Vincent Oshana, who made the video for the site Valuetainment. "Helene is an ‘extremely dangerous’ Category 4 hurricane with maximum sustained wind speeds of 130 mph, but it pales compared to Vinnie’s ex-wife," a description of the video says on Valuetainment’s site.

claim: “Olympic boxer Imane Khelif fails gender test, stripped of all titles, lifetime ban and $25 million prize money revoked!”
explanation: The International Olympic Committee’s Boxing Unit affirmed Khelif was eligible to compete in the Paris Olympics women’s boxing event. Following the controversy, neither the International Olympic Committee nor the International Boxing Association has issued any statements about a lifetime ban, revoking titles, or returning prize money. The claims stemmed from the Russian-led International Boxing Association disqualifying Khelif from competing in the 2023 World Championships after saying she failed to meet the gender eligibility requirements to compete in women’s sports following a blood test.

claim: Says Tim Walz said he carried weapons in war, but “he has not spent a day in a combat zone.”
explanation: But was what Vance said about Walz not carrying weapons in combat accurate? Vance said that Walz said he carried weapons in war, but "he has not spent a day in a combat zone." Vance attacked Tim Walz on military record.

claim: "Los 750 dólares que nuestra generosa administración ha ofrecido a las víctimas del huracán Helene son un PRÉSTAMO! Tienen un año para devolverlo".
explanation: En la mayoría de los casos, las subvenciones de FEMA NO tienen que devolverse". La "Asistencia para Necesidades Graves" de FEMA ofrece un pago único de $750 por hogar a los sobrevivientes de catástrofes que lo soliciten durante los primeros 30 días tras la declaración de la catástrofe. Algunas afirmaciones falsas se han centrado en los pagos de $750 de la Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias de Estados Unidos (FEMA, por sus siglas en inglés) para suministros esenciales.

claim: Donald Trump “intends to cut” Medicare.
explanation: In his 2024 campaign, Trump has made clear that his Medicare policy is to make no cuts. As president, though, Trump regularly proposed policies that would have reduced Medicare spending. During the 2024 presidential campaign, Trump has repeatedly said he would not cut Medicare.

claim: “Coca-Cola cuts ties with Taylor Swift over (Kamala) Harris endorsement.”
explanation: A Sept. 16 Facebook post styled to look like a news headline said, "Coca-Cola cuts ties with Taylor Swift over Harris endorsement, ‘We don’t support her endorsement.’" (Screengrab from Facebook) Users on Instagram and Threads made similar claims. We rate the claim that "Coca-Cola cuts ties with Taylor Swift over Harris endorsement" False. The Facebook post linked to an article on an unnamed website that said this endorsement prompted Coca-Cola to end its partnership with Swift because it "clashes with the brand’s values of ‘unity and neutrality.’" But the source of this claim is a satirical Facebook page called "SpaceX Fanclub."

claim: Vice President Kamala Harris is “talking about bringing back the draft.”
explanation: Even if it were to pass, however, such a provision would not bring back the draft. The provision would require women to register for the draft; it would not institute a draft. Trump said Harris is "talking about bringing back the draft."

claim: The Biden administration stole $1 billion “from FEMA to use it for illegal migrants. … And FEMA is now busted. They don’t have any money.”
explanation: The Biden-Harris administration requested the money from Congress, and Congress granted it to FEMA for the Shelter and Services program. And Trump’s administration, not Biden’s, shifted FEMA funding — including money from the Disaster Relief Fund — to address immigration. When Trump was president, his administration shifted FEMA funding, including money from the Disaster Relief Fund, to address immigration.

claim: “On (Josh) Stein’s watch, rapes in North Carolina are up 53%.”
explanation: It’s difficult to know how many rapes occurred in North Carolina under Stein’s watch because not all rapes are reported and not all rape reports lead to convictions. The claim is based on a total number of rapes reported over time — data that’s flawed because law enforcement agencies expanded their definition of what qualifies as rape while Stein was in office. The group cited North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation’s data on rape reports — data that has been affected by changes to how rape allegations are documented by law enforcement agencies.

claim: Says Kamala Harris proposed on X that “we have the next debate at a venue Donald Trump feels more comfortable: Jeffrey Epstein’s townhouse.”
explanation: So, what Harris did post July 25 about Trump and debating? We rate claims Harris wrote an X post suggesting that she and Trump debate at Epstein’s house False. A supposed X post from Harris that same day appears to show the vice president connecting Trump to the deceased financier and convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

claim: Vice President Kamala Harris responded, “Next question please,” when asked about the economy during an Aug. 29 CNN interview.
explanation: Harris says, "That’s it." And Harris said, "That’s it." Harris gave the "next question please" answer when Bash asked: "I want to ask you about your opponent, Donald Trump.

claim: "Actornautas aparecen en los videos de la NASA desde hace años mostrando el set de filmación en el supuesto alunizaje”.
explanation: Una publicación en Facebook dice que un video muestra que el primer aterrizaje a la Luna  de la NASA fue un engaño. El primer aterrizaje a la Luna si sucedió bajo la misión de Apollo 11 y el video de una supuesta actuación no es de la NASA, sino que fue creado como broma. "ACTORNAUTAS aparecen en los videos de la NASA desde hace años mostrando el set de filmación en el supuesto alunizaje", dice la publicación del 26 de mayo.

claim: Este video muestra un robo de votos en la elección del 2024 en Venezuela.
explanation: Después de la elección del 28 de julio, el Secretario de Estado de Estados Unidos, Anthony Blinken, quien estaba en Tokio, expresó preocupación de que el resultado de la elección venezolana "no refleje la voluntad o los votos del pueblo venezolano". The New York Times reportó el 28 de julio que "en algunos centros de votación clave, los funcionarios electorales se negaron a entregar los recuentos en papel a los observadores electorales" y que hubo reportes de intimidación de votantes e irregularidades. Las autoridades electorales de Venezuela declararon a Nicolás Maduro el ganador de las elecciones presidenciales del país, pero los candidatos de oposición cuestionan la integridad de los resultados.

claim: Image shows Fox Business graphic titled “Tim Walz’s Communist Agenda.”
explanation: We rate the claim that this image shows a Fox Business graphic titled "Tim Walz’s Communist Agenda" False. A social media post shared a graphic that appeared to come from Fox Business, highlighting items in Minnesota Gov. The Aug. 7 episode of "Mornings with Maria Bartiromo" did include a graphic titled "Tim Walz’s Economic Scorecard," that looked similar to the altered one.

claim: Says Democratic opponent Tammy Baldwin "gave stimulus checks to illegals."
explanation: May 2, 2022: PolitiFact rated Republican claims that U.S. Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., voted to give immigrants in the country illegally stimulus checks False. Here is a sampling: Sept. 4, 2024: PolitiFact rated Republican claims that U.S. Sen. Sherrod Brown, D-Ohio, voted to give immigrants in the country illegally stimulus checks False. April 2, 2021: Reuters rated claims that immigrants in the country illegally were eligible for stimulus checks False.

claim: Hurricane Helene was planned to seize land in North Carolina for lithium mining.
explanation: We rate the claim that Hurricane Helene was planned to seize land in North Carolina for lithium mining Pants on Fire! The claim that the government is seizing North Carolina land for lithium mining is also "false," spokespeople for the governor’s office and the state’s emergency management joint information center said. Some social media users said people engineered the hurricane to clear land in North Carolina to mine lithium, a metal used to power batteries for electric vehicles, smartphones and laptop computers.

claim: Ruben Gallego wants to “cut your Social Security.”
explanation: Johnson said the Social Security 2100 Act would significantly expand Social Security across the board. He is also backed by groups, such as the Arizona Alliance for Retired Americans and the National Committee To Preserve Social Security and Medicare, that advocate for expanding Social Security. "Kamala & Walz and Ruben Gallego want to cut your Social Security.

claim: Says Donald Trump said, “Women are miserable — not sexy, not safe.”
explanation: reads what looks like a screenshot of a Truth Social post from Trump in all caps. But a purported Truth Social post from the Republican presidential nominee that alludes to this isn’t authentic. We rate claims this is an authentic Trump post False.

claim: U.S. Sen. Jon Tester “voted to give taxpayer-funded health care to illegal immigrants."
explanation: An ad from Sheehy said Tester "voted to give taxpayer-funded health care to illegal immigrants." In 2013, during a series of budget bill amendments, Tester and other Democrats voted against a Republican-sponsored amendment that would have prohibited immigrants illegally in the country from qualifying for federally subsidized health care. But its passage would not have given "taxpayer-funded health care to illegal immigrants."

claim: “In 2021, Minnesotans were roughly five times more likely to move to Florida than vice versa” because they were “fleeing” the state under Democratic Gov. Tim Walz.
explanation: In 2021, almost four times as many Minnesotans moved to Florida than Floridians moved to Minnesota in 2021. DeSantis’ office, pointing to U.S. Census data, said that over 2021-22, "up to five people moved to Florida from Minnesota for every person moving out of Florida to Minnesota." Stefan Rayer, director of the University of Florida’s Population Program in the Bureau of Economic and Business Research, reviewed 2021 Census data and calculated that about 10,156 people moved from Minnesota to Florida and about 2,712 from Florida to Minnesota — a net gain of 7,444 people for Florida.

claim: The Federal Emergency Management Agency “is confiscating supplies and donations!”
explanation: FEMA Press Secretary Daniel Llargues told PolitiFact that claims about FEMA confiscating emergency supplies are false. FEMA is not "confiscating" emergency supplies or donations meant for Hurricane Helene survivors. FEMA officials and local and state leaders in Tennessee and North Carolina said these statements are baseless.

claim: Says John Fetterman said he’s “voting for Trump.”
explanation: "Did Fetterman just say he’s voting for Trump," a Sept. 23 Threads post said. We rate claims Fetterman said he’s voting for Trump False. Fetterman posted another photo Sept. 21 giving a thumbs-up in Indiana County, Pennsylvania.

claim: U.S. Sen. Sherrod Brown voted to “allow transgender biological men to compete in girls’ sports.”
explanation: Senate Leadership Fund Communications Director Torunn Sinclair said the amendments from Sen. Tommy Tuberville, R-Ala., hinged school funding on whether transgender women were allowed to compete in sports matching their gender identity. The amendments would have stripped federal funding from schools and colleges that allowed transgender girls and women to compete in sports matching their gender identity. He voted against two amendments to much broader spending bills that would have stripped funding from schools that allowed transgender athletes to compete in sports matching their gender identity.

claim: Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz gave a college football crowd “the bird.”
explanation: Logue told CBS News that a Vance staffer tried to negotiate with the Primanti manager, who called the restaurant’s corporate office, and Vance eventually walked back into the restaurant. "The manager told patrons, other Republicans, that Vance is not allowed to make a campaign stop at Primanti Brothers," Logue said. The video of Walz leaving the field isn’t crisp, but he’s not flipping someone off — he’s pointing.
